routeSelection.basis: Radboud currently identifies Accounting, Finance and Economics & Policy in year two and the corresponding International Economics and Policy specialisation in year three. This route best represents the generic bachelor’s broad economics, international markets and public policy identity; Accounting and Finance are narrower. The route was selected from the external programme before assessing UCR fit.

audience.programmeDescription: Economics and Business Economics studies economic decisions, firms, financial markets and societal policy. The displayed International Economics and Policy specialization combines economic theory, quantitative research, business finance and policy.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The published credit structure is shown while the thesis-entry conditions for the renewed curriculum are clarified. UCR comparisons are withheld pending that clarification.

curriculum.routeLabel: International Economics and Policy; curriculum for 2025 entrants
curriculum.limitation: The listed components total 180 EC, but the prerequisite relationship for the required thesis remains unresolved. This is a supported credit structure rather than a certified complete pathway.

componentNotes.y3-electives: 24 EC of approved choice, normally 18 EC in period 1 and 6 EC in period 4. Courses outside the programme require approval and must not overlap. Master’s and applied-science courses are normally excluded; exceptions for study abroad follow the learning agreement. An optional 12 EC internship may replace two 6 EC electives.
componentNotes.y3-thesis: Required 12 EC economics research project. The formal entry rule names earlier methods courses whose relationship to the renewed curriculum needs authoritative clarification.
componentNotes.y1-academic: Academic and professional skills are compulsory. The linked academic-language test adds no credits. First-year study advice normally requires 42 of 60 EC, subject to personal circumstances.
